articles.title: Switch or rename a workspace
articles.summary: Each workspace has its own inboxes, API keys and members. Switch at the top of the sidebar.
articles.keywords: workspace switch change rename name sidebar menu workspaces client business
steps: Click the workspace name at the top of the sidebar.
Pick another workspace under Workspaces.
To rename it, open Settings and edit Workspace name, then Save changes.
Only the owner or an admin can rename a workspace.

articles.title: Create another workspace
articles.summary: Extra workspaces are a Team feature. A new workspace inherits your plan.
articles.keywords: new workspace create add second client business team plan multiple workspaces
steps: Click the workspace name at the top of the sidebar.
Choose New workspace.
Enter a Workspace name and choose Create workspace.
body: Your plan belongs to your account, so every workspace you own shares it. On other plans, New workspace links to the plans instead.

articles.title: Invite someone to your workspace
articles.summary: Owners and admins invite people from Members. Inviting needs the Team plan.
articles.keywords: invite member colleague collaborator team add user seat email resend cancel invite
steps: Open Members.
Under Invite a collaborator, enter their email address and pick a role.
Choose Send invite. The accept link is valid for 7 days.
If the email did not arrive, choose Resend on the pending invite.
To withdraw it, choose Cancel invite.

articles.title: Accept a workspace invite
articles.summary: Open the link in the invite email and sign in with the address the invite was sent to.
articles.keywords: accept invite join workspace invitation link expired different email wrong account
steps: Open the accept link in the invite email within 7 days.
Sign in or sign up with the exact address the invite was sent to.
Link expired? Ask an owner or admin to choose Resend. Older links then stop working.

articles.title: What each member role can do
articles.summary: Owner, Admin, Member and Viewer. Viewers can only read.
articles.keywords: role roles permissions owner admin member viewer read only access rights
steps: Owner: full control, including billing, deleting the workspace and changing roles.
Admin: invites and removes members and renames the workspace.
Member: connects mailboxes, edits signatures, creates API keys and runs automations.
Viewer: read only. Their API keys can only use read tools.

articles.title: Change a role, remove a member or leave
articles.summary: Changes take effect at once. Removed or departing members lose their API keys for the workspace.
articles.keywords: change role remove member kick leave workspace revoke access promote demote
steps: In Members, the owner changes roles in the Role column.
Remove someone with the button on their row, then confirm Remove member.
Admins can remove members and viewers, but not other admins.
To leave a workspace you were invited to, choose Leave workspace.
The owner cannot leave. Delete the workspace in Settings instead.

articles.title: Change your name, email or language
articles.summary: Edit your profile and dashboard language in Settings, under Account.
articles.keywords: profile display name email address change language locale norsk settings account
steps: Open Settings.
Edit Display name and choose Save changes.
Choose Change email and enter the new address.
Click the confirmation link sent to the new address to finish.
Pick a language under Language.

articles.title: Change or reset your password
articles.summary: Change it in Settings, or reset it from Forgot password? on the sign-in page.
articles.keywords: password change reset forgot sign in login magic link google github
steps: In Settings, fill in Current password and New password, then Update password.
Use at least 8 characters.
Forgot it? Choose Forgot password? on the sign-in page. The link lasts 60 minutes.
You can also sign in with Google, GitHub or a magic link.

articles.title: Sign out your other devices
articles.summary: Security lists every device signed in to your account. You stay signed in on this one.
articles.keywords: sessions devices sign out log out other devices browsers security stolen laptop
steps: Open Security.
Check the list under Active sessions.
Choose the sign-out button there to end every session except this one.

articles.title: See which tool calls ran
articles.summary: The audit log on Security lists every MCP tool call, with its inbox, API key and status.
articles.keywords: audit log activity history tool calls who what when api key security trail
steps: Open Security.
Scroll to Audit log.
Each row shows the tool, inbox, API key, status, timestamp and duration.
body: The log never records email subjects, bodies or recipients.

articles.title: Choose the right plan
articles.summary: Count the people who sign in first, then the mailboxes.
articles.keywords: plan plans free personal pro team compare which plan inboxes seats upgrade price
steps: Free: one inbox and 150 email actions a month.
Personal: up to 3 inboxes and no monthly action cap.
Pro: unlimited inboxes for one person.
Team: more than one login, with roles and a workspace per client.
See Pricing for prices and the full comparison.

articles.title: What a plan or billing change costs
articles.summary: You see the exact charge and confirm it before anything changes.
articles.keywords: upgrade downgrade switch plan annual monthly yearly interval proration credit charge payment not completed declined invoice
steps: In Settings, under Billing & plan, pick Monthly or Annual, then the plan's Get button.
New subscribers pay on Stripe. Existing subscribers see the charge first, then confirm.
A plan change is prorated. Your renewal date stays the same.
Switching monthly and annual credits unused time. Your billing period restarts that day.
Payment not completed? Your plan is unchanged. Choose Pay invoice to finish.

articles.title: What we store about your email
articles.summary: Email content is never stored, except messages you schedule. Mailbox passwords are encrypted.
articles.keywords: privacy data stored storage encryption encrypted gdpr eu training credentials password token delete export
steps: Mail your assistant reads or sends now is fetched live and never stored.
A scheduled message is stored until it is sent, then kept as history.
Mailbox passwords and tokens are encrypted with AES-256-GCM.
Account data is stored in the EU. Your email never trains AI models.
To request a copy of your data, write to us.

articles.title: Host MCP Emails yourself
articles.summary: It is open source (AGPL-3.0) and runs with docker-compose, for IMAP and SMTP mailboxes.
articles.keywords: self host self-host open source agpl docker docker-compose own server on premise
body: Your credentials are encrypted under a key only you hold. Gmail and Outlook sign-in and the dashboard stay on the hosted service.
